## Each party's obligations

| Party | Obligation | Deadline / trigger | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Harrow & Finch Ltd (Employer) | Pay compensation of £18,500 for loss of employment | Within 14 days of receiving the agreement signed by Maya Bennett and her adviser | Term 1, table |
| Harrow & Finch Ltd (Employer) | Pay a legal fees contribution of £750 | 14 days after signature | Table only |
| Harrow & Finch Ltd (Employer) | Provide a reference in agreed wording | On request | Term 2 |
| Maya Bennett (Employee) | Sign the agreement and have her adviser sign it | Before payment is triggered | Term 1 (implied) |
| Maya Bennett (Employee) | Withdraw tribunal claim 6001842/2026 | Within 7 days of receiving payment | Term 3 |
| Maya Bennett (Employee) | Keep the terms confidential, except for disclosure to Daniel Bennett, professional advisers, or as required by law | Ongoing | Term 4 |
| Maya Bennett (Employee) | Return laptop, security pass and Employer documents | By 31 October 2026 | Term 5 |

## Risks for the Employee

- **The agreement may not be a valid statutory settlement agreement.** UK law sets conditions for an agreement that settles employment claims. These include identifying the adviser, confirming the adviser is insured, and stating that the statutory conditions are met. Only the first is covered here, so the agreement's legal effect may be uncertain.
- **The "without prejudice and subject to contract" heading.** If the heading stays on the signed version, Harrow & Finch Ltd could argue no binding contract was formed. That would make the payment harder to enforce.
- **The reference wording isn't attached.** Term 2 promises a reference in "agreed wording," but no wording is set out or annexed. This leaves room for dispute or an unhelpful reference.
- **The legal fees contribution is only in the table.** £750 appears in the payment table but in none of the numbered terms. It also doesn't say who receives it, which is usually the adviser directly. That makes it weaker to enforce.
- **The payment deadlines don't match.** Term 1 runs from when Harrow & Finch Ltd *receives* the signed agreement, while the table says "after signature." There's also no remedy if payment is late.
- **Tax treatment is unclear.** The agreement doesn't say whether £18,500 is paid gross or net. Compensation for loss of employment may be tax-free only up to a threshold, and any part treated as notice pay is taxable. The amount she actually receives could be less than expected.
- **The confidentiality clause is one-sided.** It binds only Maya Bennett. Harrow & Finch Ltd has no matching duty of confidentiality and no promise not to make negative comments about her.
- **The confidentiality exceptions are narrow.** They don't expressly cover protected disclosures (whistleblowing), reporting to police or regulators, medical or tax advisers, or close family other than Daniel Bennett. Some of these rights can't be removed by law anyway, but leaving them out could discourage her from using them or lead to arguments about breach.
- **There's no release by the Employer.** Maya Bennett gives up her claim, but Harrow & Finch Ltd doesn't give up any claims it might have against her.
- **Other entitlements aren't mentioned.** Final salary, accrued holiday pay, pension contributions and benefits aren't addressed. Harrow & Finch Ltd could argue these are covered by the settlement sum.
- **The property return term is vague.** Term 5 is passive ("will be returned"), with no process for wiping personal data from the laptop and no stated consequence if items are late. A dispute here could be used to delay or challenge payment.
- **Standard protective clauses are missing.** There's no entire-agreement clause, governing law clause, or statement of what happens if either side breaches. That adds uncertainty if anything goes wrong.

I'm not a lawyer, so treat this as a starting checklist rather than advice. Priya Shah of Elm Row Legal LLP, who is named as her adviser, is the right person to confirm these points and negotiate changes before she signs.
